transcript: Solution engineer: What is the problem at self-checkout?
Loss prevention manager: Non-scans. Items go into the bag without going over the scanner. We know it happens, we catch almost none of it.
Store operations director: And when we do catch it, the confrontation at the till is worse for the brand than the loss.
Solution engineer: What do you want the system to do?
Loss prevention manager: Flag a likely non-scan in real time so an attendant can walk over and help. Politely.
Store operations director: I would rather have an end-of-day review of clips, no real-time interruptions. Real time will create incidents.
Loss prevention manager: End of day is useless. The customer has left.
Solution engineer: I will note both positions, that needs a decision from you. What cameras exist?
IT integration lead: Each self-checkout has an overhead camera already, installed by the till vendor. We can get the streams. The till also sends a scan event with a timestamp.
Solution engineer: So the signal is a bag movement without a scan event close to it.
Loss prevention manager: Exactly, and the weight sensor already does some of this and gets ignored because it is wrong so often.
Store manager: Attendants switch the weight alerts off by ten in the morning. Whatever you build has to be better than that or it goes the same way.
Solution engineer: How many tills and stores?
Store operations director: One pilot store, eight self-checkouts. It is our busiest.
Solution engineer: Success?
Loss prevention manager: Known shrink at that store versus the same period last year. We have the number.
Store operations director: And attendant complaints. If they hate it, it fails, whatever the shrink says.
Solution engineer: Privacy?
IT integration lead: Cameras are already signposted for security. Clips cannot leave the country and we keep them thirty days unless there is an incident.
Store manager: Staff will ask whether it is watching them. It should not be.
Loss prevention manager: It is not about staff. Customers only.
Solution engineer: Who reviews flagged events?
Store manager: The duty manager, whichever of us is on. There is no dedicated person.
Solution engineer: Understood. Anything else discussed?
Store operations director: Queue length prediction. Another time.

traps.note: Real-time flags (L5) versus end-of-day review only (L6).
The real-time versus end-of-day decision was explicitly deferred to the customer.
